title: Exaion signs $79m GPUaaS contract with US customer
html:
French AI cloud provider Exaion has secured a US customer under a four-year contract, while US-based AI cloud company QumulusAI has secured 2MW of colocation capacity.

Under Exaion's agreement, it will provide GPU-as-a-Service in a 100 percent take-or-pay contract valued at $79 million.

Exaion will provide compute powered by Nvidia HGX B300 servers for the customer. In a LinkedIn post, the company said: "Mara provides the energy-backed infrastructure, and Exaion turns it into compute and cloud services, from private cloud infrastructure to inference as a service for customers who need greater control over their data. It is also a signal of demand. Exaion’s customers and prospects have expressed demand for more than 30MW of compute capacity for delivery by the end of 2027."

Mara Holdings, a digital energy and infrastructure company known for its cryptomining operations, along with EDF Pulse Ventures, acquired Exaion in August 2025.

Mara is one of the biggest Bitcoin miners in the US, predominantly utilizing stranded energy assets to power modular mining units. In April 2025, the company fully energized a 25MW modular cryptomine data center powered by flared natural gas in Texas and North Dakota. In December 2024, the company acquired an onshore wind farm with plans to develop and operate a Bitcoin mining operation on the site, powered behind-the-meter.

Founded in 2020, Exaion launched its first data center in Sherbrooke, Canada, in 2024. Spanning 4,000 sq ft (372 sqm), the Tier II quality facility offers 780kW of capacity. The site is home to a quantum computer from Quandela.

As of February 2026, Exaion operated four data centers across Canada and France.

QumulusAI secures 2MW of colocation capacity

US-based AI cloud company QumulusAI, meanwhile, has signed a ten-year colocation agreement for 2MW of capacity in the northeastern US. The contract has two three-year renewal options.

QumulusAI said the capacity is expected to be ready for service by the end of 2026, and the company has a right of first offer on a further 9.6MW at the site.

The company is funding the first phase from cash generated by capacity already in production.

“The first 2MW is scheduled for service by the end of this year, which is weeks away, not quarters,” said Michael Maniscalco, CEO of QumulusAI. “That is capacity we can put in front of customers now, with the possibility to take significantly more at the same site.”

Earlier this month, QumulusAI expanded its capacity in Denver, Colorado, by 1.2MW under a five-year agreement, with automatic five-year renewal terms for the colocation capacity. It is expected to be operational from Q1 2027.
summary: While QumulusAI secures 2MW of colocation capacity
